E1.evidence:
Reproducer in the issue body: "- Start two gazebo kobukis (segbot + kobuki is ok)
- Send commands to cmd_vel of one kobuki
- KGP catches these and moves around properly in gazebo world
- **KGP does not post rotations to the odom topic (translations are there)**
- **KGP does not publish rotation information on base_footprint-odom tf.**"; diagnosis by slivingston: "The bug is due to the different Kobuki plugins using the same ImuSensor."; fix merged as PR #39 and confirmed by the maintainer.

E2.evidence: Step 1: the units are two deployed instances of the gazebo_ros_kobuki model plugin (package kobuki_gazebo_plugins), one per spawned robot model, both loaded into the same Gazebo process; they interact through Gazebo's global sensor registry. Step 2: the failure occurs only when a second instance is present ("there is apparently correct behavior in the case of a single Kobuki"): each instance resolves its IMU with the unscoped name 'imu' (sensors::SensorManager::Instance()->GetSensor(imu_name) at gazebo_ros_kobuki_loads.cpp:298), so both bind the same ImuSensor object and one robot's orientation is read from the other's sensor; the failure depends on the peer instance, so not internal. Step 3: the resolving change is in the plugin's code (fully scoped lookup), not a launch or parameter binding. Steps 4-5 do not apply. Interface kind: exclusive resource (the Gazebo sensor named 'imu', which each instance must own exclusively).

E3.evidence: CONCURRENT: two instances of the plugin active at the same time in one simulation ("Start two gazebo kobukis"); a single instance works.

E4.evidence: Observed failure: "KGP does not post rotations to the odom topic (translations are there)" and "KGP does not publish rotation information on base_footprint-odom tf."

units.name: kobuki_gazebo_plugins (model instance 1)
units.revision_basis: 06d8fa71 is tag 0.4.1 (2014-09-19, indigo), the parent of the fix merge and the revision slivingston's diagnosis links for the unscoped lookup ("line 289 of gazebo_ros_kobuki_loads.cpp" at 06d8fa71); the report (2014-09-23) names no revision, and this is the release current on the report date. 4115400a is the merge of PR #39 (commit 494e7370, 'kobuki_gazebo_plugins: Resolve IMU sensor using fully scoped name') into indigo on 2015-03-02, contained in tag 0.4.2 (same day).

units.name: kobuki_gazebo_plugins (model instance 2)
units.revision_basis: Same package and revisions as instance 1: both robots are spawned from the same kobuki_gazebo.urdf.xacro and load the same libgazebo_ros_kobuki plugin; the reporter's second model ("segbot + kobuki is ok") also embeds the Kobuki plugin.

failed_conditions.quote: The basic problem is that the sensor name, as obtained on [line 289 of gazebo_ros_kobuki_loads.cpp](https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki_desktop/blob/06d8fa710928ba5623939ce42f760838cd0f4667/kobuki_gazebo_plugins/src/gazebo_ros_kobuki_loads.cpp#L289) is not scoped. Thus it is the same when multiple models are spawned using the same URDF file, namely kobuki_gazebo.urdf.xacro, which declares the imu name [at line 186](https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki/blob/06e60c2bba4c73699f69ffc61250f1ad152a931a/kobuki_description/urdf/kobuki_gazebo.urdf.xacro#L186). Hence, the sensor obtained by `sensors::SensorManager::Instance()->GetSensor()` is subject to a race condition.

loudness_evidence: "KGP does not post rotations to the odom topic (translations are there)" and "KGP does not publish rotation information on base_footprint-odom tf." (https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki_desktop/issues/38): the second instance's GetSensor('imu') succeeds and returns the other model's sensor, so no error is raised (the plugin's 'Couldn't find the IMU in the model!' branch is not taken); the wrong orientation is only visible in the published data.

resolution.summary: In GazeboRosKobuki::prepareIMU() resolve the IMU with its fully scoped name, sensors::get_sensor(world_->GetName()+"::"+node_name_+"::base_footprint::"+imu_name), instead of SensorManager::Instance()->GetSensor(imu_name), so each plugin instance binds the sensor of its own model (PR #39, commit 494e7370, merged as 4115400a).
resolution.evidence: Maintainer jihoonl on PR #39: "I have confirmed that it resolves #38. Thanks @slivingston!!!" (https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki_desktop/pull/39#issuecomment-76671612), and on the issue: "This has been resolved witih #39" (https://github.com/yujinrobot/kobuki_desktop/issues/38#issuecomment-76671649); resolved composition = two instances of kobuki_gazebo_plugins at 4115400a (PR head 494e7370 merged into indigo).

notes: Alternative framing: kobuki_gazebo_plugins (consumer) against Gazebo's sensors API (provider), where GetSensor(name) with an unscoped name returns the first registered match; recorded as two co-active plugin instances because the failure only exists with a second model and the reporter's report is 'Multi-Gazebo Kobukis'. The name 'imu' is declared by a third, unchanged unit, kobuki_description's kobuki_gazebo.urdf.xacro (kobuki 06e60c2b: line 148 '<sensor type="imu" name="imu">' under gyro_link and line 186 '<imu_name>imu</imu_name>' passed to the plugin); the resolved lookup scopes it under '::base_footprint::' because Gazebo merges the fixed-joint links into base_footprint. The bumper and the three cliff sensors are resolved by the same unscoped GetSensor(name) calls at 06d8fa71 (lines 216-220, 271) and are listed in the inventory as shared names; no failure of theirs is documented and the fix does not change them. An earlier patch in the thread (tf::Quaternion::setRPY instead of setEuler in gazebo_ros_kobuki_updates.cpp) was tested and found "not sufficient" and is not part of the resolution. Issue #31 (tf_prefix / odom namespacing for multiple models) is a related but separate composition. The related Gazebo Answers thread on multiple robots with sensor plugins (http://answers.gazebosim.org/question/4878/) was linked but not fetched. The PR was made against the indigo branch and the concert examples in the thread are indigo; the reporter does not state the distro, so ros_distro is left null.
